summary:
RANKED JEV CAPABILITIES (best to worst; number → source).

1. Yes/no on literal, verifiable facts present in the state. "Does the text mention X" 0.983 acc / Brier 0.013; NLI entailment 0.980; world facts 0.967; no item wrong at p ≥ 0.9 or ≤ 0.1; clear items 30/30 identical on repeat (REPORT.md §9 l.198-216, §6 l.131-147). Reading code-computed numbers back: program_correct / made_progress / broke_something 240/240 each at 0.5 with counts+lists in state (Brier ≤ 0.008, AUROC 1.0) (probe-progress-judgment.md Part 1). Best primitive when the answer is a fact in the state; useless when the fact must be derived.

2. Choosing among ≤ 255 concrete, informative options when the correct one is present and N is small. 12-way topic Choice 96/96 with confidence ≥ 0.95 on 90; city→country over 200 options 100 % at mean conf 0.997 (REPORT §8 l.194, §10 l.249). Anchor selection 14/14 among 2-4 mutants, P(correct) 0.81-1.00 (anchor-probe.md). Donor line among own-program lines 35/36 (P p50 0.98), 33/36 at 25-76 options, 32/36 at 254 (probe-donor-and-templates.md headline 1a-1c). Identifier hole filling 13/13 leak-free (2a/2b). Insertion point given the statement 4/4, condition line given the condition 4/4 (4a/4b). QuixBugs fix Choice N=10 36/40 top-1, 40/40 top-3 (probe-selection.md Summary). Selection with the unchanged buggy line removed: 19/20 top-1, 20/20 test-passing top pick, 0 confident misses (probe-question-design.md S_no_unchanged / S_combo_no_unchanged).

3. Ranking many near-duplicate candidate lines (Nouls per candidate, one request). Full-criteria Nouls top-1 39/39/35/31 of 40 and top-3 40/40/39/39 at N=10/50/150/254; compact Nouls top-1 39/37/32/32, top-3 40/40/38/36; flat Choice top-1 36/31/29/26, top-3 40/40/38/37 (probe-selection.md Summary and Nouls table). Two-stage Nouls(254)→Choice(top-5) 33/40 with fix shortlisted 39/40. Developer fix among mean 295 depth-1 candidates: Noul top-1 26/34, top-5 31/34, MRR 0.83 (lit-search-based-repair.md §7). Live engine: gold ranked first p 0.97-1.00 at every ladder `account` site (jev-only-ladder-4-analysis.md §1.2); `ranking_missed` = 0 on rung 1a (jev-only-rungs-1-2.md §1). Decay with N is intrinsic (95 % → 72 % without escape); order-sensitive at ties (reshuffle moved `kth` 0.48 → 0.14, `next_permutation` 0.19 → 0.52; lit-search-based-repair.md verification).

4. Arbitration among test-passing candidates (behaviour clusters). Choice = gold 8/10, gold-or-equivalent 10/10 at the true line; cross-line 10/14 and 13/14; all-overfit set rejected at P(escape) 0.90 / max Noul 0.06; $0.0008-0.0015, p50 189-219 ms (experiments/contrarian/run-arbitrate-{truth,all}.log; results/contrarian-arbitrate.*.jsonl). Advisory only: gold Noul 0.15 on `quicksort`, below 0.7 on 4/10 (guard.ts:86-110 constants).

5. Localisation from failure evidence. Repo-wide file Nouls from issue text alone (61-778 files, ≤ 4 requests): gold #1 23/30, ≤ 5 28/30, ≤ 10 30/30, MRR 0.85, $0.0011/instance (probe-swebench-understanding.md Q6). Package Nouls with outlines gold-first 31/33 (Q3). Choice over ~219 files 24/30 top-1, 30/30 top-5 (probe-localization.md §6); Noul-per-file over 60 is calibrated: p ≥ 0.7 → 23/26 gold vs base rate 2.1 %, Brier 0.010 (§6.2). Function stage top-1 19/37 (51 %), top-5 35/37 (Q2); line ±3 top-5 94 % (80 % if escape-dominated rows count as misses) (Q4); chained file#1 ∧ fn≤5 ∧ line≤5 21/30. QuixBugs line Choice with the buggy program's actual output: top-1 28/40, top-3 36/40, MRR 0.805, +5 over tests-only 23/40 in every run; D∪C top-3 covers 38/40 (probe-localization.md §1, §3). Traceback-frame Noul: top frame in the gold file 3/3 (oracle-from-issue.md). Weak on insertion bugs (0/4 top-1 in every variant) and "innocent-looking" lines (`lis`, `mergesort` at p ≤ 0.03 with 0.7-0.9 on a wrong line; §5).

6. Judging which extracted snippet reproduces an issue. is_reproduction ≥ 0.5 set = hand labels 18/23, shows_expected 20/23, failure_kind 21/23; valid oracle on 9/30 SWE instances for $0.0096 total (oracle-from-issue.md headline).

7. Progress judgment — solved but redundant. 240/240 only when `passed/failed/total/newly_passing/newly_failing` are in the state; with raw failure lists only, made_progress hedges 0.40-0.46 on 1-more-test partials and broke_something misses 14/76 regressions (probe-progress-judgment.md Part 1 `raw`); a free next-move Choice misread 1/7→2/7 as "did not help" on 6/10 partials (Part 2 A) → Q17 deleted, code routes 240/240 (DECISIONS.md l.456).

8. Judging an LLM's plans/actions (jev-on mode) — measured only indirectly, no accuracy gain. Paired 29 SWE tasks: jev-on 9/29 vs jev-off 10/29; 208 blocks + 170 declined reviews; completion Noul rarely reached 0.85 so solved runs hit the 25-step cap with a correct patch on disk; intent Choice often `finish`/`edit` with paired Noul < 0.5 → fallback; 18 % fewer generator tokens/step and reads 83 vs 124 (docs/STATUS.md l.68-101; DESIGN.md §17 l.2377-2388). First live slice: 14/25 steps in review on `plan_mismatch` at confidence 0.00 before the alignment-dimension mapping fix (DECISIONS.md l.196-206). No labelled set exists for plan-judgment accuracy.

9. Abstract-kind classification — weak, never a gate. SWE change-kind 16/30 strict (53 %), 22/30 lenient (probe-swebench-understanding.md Q1); QuixBugs fix-kind 25/40 → 30/40 with the line named (probe-donor §3); Q7 edit_class with clean examples 24/40 top-1, 34-35/40 top-2 (experiments/inspect/out/q7-clean-live-run{1,2}.json; the earlier 28-29/40 was contaminated by ten quoted gold fixes, jev-only-audit.md §3.2). Fine when categories are disjoint (topics 100 %), poor when they overlap.

10. Building a line by a sequence of Choices (generation as search). Teacher-forced next token 84.3 % top-1 / 96.2 % top-3 (probe-token-synthesis.md T1); free-running W=3 + grammar filter 20/40 lines at $0.0037 and 3.3 s/line; portfolio 27-28/40 (T4, §7). Slot fill 90-93 % top-1; diff-fill 23/25 (92 %) at B=3, full-fill 22/29 (76 %) (lit-guided-synthesis.md §5.2). Sketch Choice top-1 23-26/40, top-3 29-31/40, coverage 39/40 (grammar-synthesis.md Appendix A.2). 58/67 teacher-forced misses are skip-ahead (right token, wrong cursor position). Text generation itself is impossible (REPORT §1): only ≤ 255 code-proposed options per decision.

11. "Fix not in set" detection — soft routing signal only. P(escape) − p_max ≥ 0.10: AUROC 0.916, 82 % detection / 13 % false alarm pooled, decaying 98 % → 73 % from N=10 to 254; Nouls max < 0.5: 71-75 % / 16-21 % (probe-selection.md detector tables). Escape alone wins 9/36 when the donor is absent, escape-or-buggy-line 35/36 (probe-donor 1d); escape 5/23 when the buggy line's template is in the pool (probe-token-synthesis T5). In RANK mode on SWE, 152/160 `fix` Choices answered `none_of_these` and the test-passing line sat at p 0.03-0.31 (jev-only-rungs-1-2.md §21.6 item 3).

12. Counting, arithmetic, dates, positional indirection — bad. r in strawberry Choice "3" at 0.52 (wrong), 1000 vs 1011 "within 1 %" 0.73 (wrong), mixed date formats 0.32 (wrong), "two positions before the last" 0.25 (wrong) (REPORT §10 l.226-232); order-only option keys collapse to 4-5/20 top-1 (probe-question-design.md Lb_opaque_nodesc); position-indexed edit-site keys give the weakest route (edit beam 5/36 exact). Verifying a stated arithmetic fact works (17×23=391 at 1.00).

CALIBRATION/THRESHOLDS THAT WORKED: Choice P(top) ≥ 0.9 → 92 % right on line localisation (58/63), 0.7-0.9 bin only 62 % (probe-localization.md §4); Noul-per-line p ≥ 0.9 → 17/17; selection Choice with actual output P(top) ≥ 0.7 → precision 0.98-1.00, Noul with criteria ≥ 0.5 → 48/48 (probe-question-design.md §3 threshold table, §7); next-token p(top) ≥ 0.9 → 99 % (100/101), < 0.6 → 42-60 % (probe-token-synthesis T2); repo file Nouls consumed by rank not threshold (precision 0.54 at 0.5, 0.79 at 0.7, 0.92 at 0.9 with recall 0.32); sketch P(top) ≥ 0.5 → top-3 25/27 vs 4/13 below; all-overfit signature escape ≥ 0.5 ∧ max Noul < 0.1 (gold sets had escape ≤ 0.38 and a Noul ≥ 0.45; guard.ts:86-88); override rule 0.3/0.7 advisory; risk mapping harm = max(E[k]/(n−1), P(k≥3)), alignment = P(k≥3) only, block ≥ 0.7 / review ≥ 0.3 (DESIGN.md §5.3).

LATENCY/COST: single request p50 167 ms, p90 252, p99 289; flat in question count (1,000 Nouls 466 ms); state 30k tokens 372 ms; 128-way concurrency 166 req/s, 0×429 in 2,500 calls (REPORT §5). Probes p50 176-253 ms, p95 319-519; 254 full-criteria Nouls p50 547 / p95 785; 300-Noul batches p50 325 / p95 565. Live engine p50/p95: QuixBugs final 178/340 ms (n=1,225), ladder 191/342 (n=2,151), SWE jev-only 227/541 (n=3,222), jev-on 237/547 (n=2,719). Cost = input_tokens × 4.2e-8 exactly ($0.042/M, output free): ~1k-token request $0.00004 = $0.04 per 1k requests; 254-option Choice $0.30/1k; compact 254 Nouls $0.77/1k; full-criteria 254 Nouls $2.40/1k; engine averages $0.15/1k (QuixBugs, ladder), $0.40/1k (SWE jev-only), $0.57/1k (jev-on, context Nouls over 300 files dominate at 28,351 Jev tokens/step).

reusable_for_llm_jev: REPORT §1: Jev does not generate text; exactly three primitives (Noul yes/no, Choice ≤ 255 options, Score ≤ 10 levels) and nothing else is accepted.
REPORT §14: Treat Jev as a fast, calibrated classifier over YOUR options, not a reasoner; clear judgments come back 0.99/0.01 with zero noise, hedged ones sit mid-band with ±0.02 noise.
REPORT §6/§14: Never threshold at 0.5 on anything borderline (sd 0.020-0.026 in 0.55-0.80; a 0.5 cut flips between runs); route the 0.3-0.7 band to a human, a bigger model, tests, or a wider search.

REPORT §4/§7/§14: Batch every question about one state into one request (13 questions: 617 vs 5,609 tokens, 161 vs 2,731 ms, answers within 0.01); latency is flat in question count; questions are independent and ids are invisible to the model.

REPORT §10/§11/§14: Name the target with a backticked path when the state holds more than one candidate (vague wording drifted 0.28/0.15/0.10 with distractors, path-named stayed 0.01-0.02); context rot is ambiguity of reference, not length (30k filler: no drift).

REPORT §10/§14: Always give a Choice an escape option (`none_of_these: null`) or pair it with per-option Nouls; a Choice is relative and always picks something (0.88 on an irrelevant option while Nouls said 0.02-0.05).

REPORT §10/§14: Do arithmetic, counting, date comparison, numeric closeness and positional lookup in code and put the numbers in the state; let Jev extract parts (month/day) or verify a stated fact. Extends to list-set differences (probe-progress-judgment raw variant).

REPORT §11/§14: Write criteria as definition plus examples, both sides (0.55 → 0.70 → 0.80 on subtle items); it is the biggest accuracy lever and the defence against keyword flooding (0.66-0.90 → 0.13-0.30).

REPORT §8/§14: Compute your own confidence from `probabilities`: Choice (p_max − 1/n)/(1 − 1/n); Score 1 − E|k − argmax|/U_n; Noul has none (harness uses |2p − 1|); confidence tracks peakedness, not correctness (chroma at 0.83 among irrelevant options).

REPORT §14 / clean/models: Pin the dated id typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917 for reproducible thresholds; the response `model` field reports the dated id; log `id`/`x-generation-id` per decision because generation lookup returns 404.

REPORT §10/§11: Score levels are situations, not degrees; one quantity per Score (a mixed severity+mood rubric split 0.33/0.67 at confidence 0.50 where the one-dimensional version gave 1.0; numeric-only levels drift to the top).
REPORT §10/§11: Write Nouls so `true` is the condition you want to detect and keep instruction and criteria aligned (swapped descriptions 0.96 → 0.88; contradictory instruction vs criteria 0.02).

REPORT §7/§10: Option keys carry a name prior (`a`/`alpha`/`1` took 0.53-0.91 with null descriptions): use semantic snake_case keys plus descriptions (0.98) over opaque keys plus descriptions (0.96) over bare semantic keys (0.91); duplicate descriptions split the mass (0.42/0.57).
REPORT §11: Prefer a 5-way Choice over a single Noul for graded judgments (0.85 vs 0.55 accuracy).
REPORT §6: Noul is clipped to [0.01, 0.99]; treat ≥ 0.98 as saturated yes and ≤ 0.02 as saturated no; Choice and Score probabilities do reach exactly 0 and 1.

REPORT §10: State is data, not hostile by default: instruction injection is nearly inert (+0.01 to +0.05) but keyword pressure and argumentative text move the answer unless criteria pin the definition — tool output and repo files are attacker-controlled.
REPORT §10: With an empty or silent state Jev answers from its weights (world-knowledge prior); never rely on it.
REPORT §11: Adding 'Answer carefully and literally' helps tricky fact questions (0.923 → 0.962); putting content in `instructions` vs `state` is equivalent, in `criteria` is worse (0.61).
REPORT §11: Decide thresholds from your own confidence-vs-accuracy plot, never from the docs' illustrative 0.5/0.6/0.7/0.8/0.9 values.

REPORT §7: Option order does not matter with informative options (0 flips on 20 items × 3 orders), but with hundreds of near-duplicate code lines order/key assignment moves mid-band items by up to 0.3 (lit-search-based-repair verification) — re-ask shuffled when the top-2 margin is < 0.1.

REPORT §3/§5: Limits and throughput to design around: 255 options, 10 levels, 32k tokens state + longest question, 64k per request, 1,000 Nouls in one request answered in 466 ms, 128-way concurrency at 166 req/s with 0 × 429 in 2,500 calls.

REPORT §2/§13 + RESEARCH §5.2: Through OpenRouter expect 400 (Zod array or TypeSafe `detail`) not 422, 524 on oversize, 529 overloaded; adopted retry = 3 attempts, retry 408/429/5xx-except-501 and fetch failures, never 400-404, backoff min(500·2^(n−1), 5000) ms with subtract-only jitter, 10 s per attempt, 30 s per decision, $1.00 per-run cap.

REPORT §9/§14 + probes: Use Jev's probabilities as a RANKER feeding a cheap verifier (tests), not as a verdict: AUROC ≈ 1.0 even where the 0.5 cut is 55 % accurate; on code, walk candidates in probability order and let tests decide.
DESIGN.md §5.4 rule 3: Every non-escape Choice option gets a paired absolute Noul `can_<option>` and code reconciles them (Choice resolution); Jev is never asked to reconcile its own answers.

DESIGN.md §5.4 rule 5 / probe-progress-judgment: Test counts, byte sizes, step counts, diff stats, 'did tests run after the last edit', newly_passing/newly_failing are computed in code and placed in the state as fields; the same numbers are then read back by Jev at 240/240 — so do not spend a request re-deriving them.

probe-question-design §7: The candidate-set shape matters more than the wording: never include the unchanged buggy line as a candidate (confident-wrong attractor); include expected AND actual output; keep candidates as a JSON object keyed by option key (a single string state drops selection to 11/20); do not add prose specs/docstrings (hurt 17 → 14.25/20).

probe-localization §8 / probe-question-design: Always execute the failing test and put the actual outcome in words in the state ('did not finish within 2 seconds (probable infinite loop)'); input/expected pairs without actual output add nothing to localisation.

probe-selection §What this means: Above ~10 candidates rank with one Noul per candidate in one request rather than a flat Choice; stay near 50 candidates by localising first; batch larger pools as parallel 50-254-Noul requests (128-way concurrency), not one 254-Choice.

probe-swebench-understanding §What this means: Consume repo-wide file Nouls by rank (top-5 beam), not by threshold (precision 0.54 at 0.5, 0.79 at 0.7, 0.92 at 0.9 with recall 0.32); confirm the beam with symbol outlines; never gate candidate sources on a change-kind Choice (53 %).

contrarian/judge2 + guard.ts: Where a verification (test run) is cheap, exhaust instead of rank; use Jev to order the queue when runs cost seconds, and to arbitrate only among behaviour-clustered test-passing candidates; keep every acceptance Noul advisory (gold Nouls reach 0.15).

Q7 edit_class wording quoted ten QuixBugs gold fixes verbatim; the cited 28-29/40 was contaminated and the clean number is 24/40 top-1 (audit §3.2; q7-clean-live-run*.json) — any Jev question wording must be checked against benchmark gold before its accuracy is quoted.

The escape option costs 2-3/40 top-1 at every N on borderline items and the decay with N (95 % → 72 %) is intrinsic; the escape also fires on genuine one-line bugs (longest_common_subsequence at 0.30-0.47 in every localisation run; SWE none_of_these at 0.60-0.82 on two instances) so it must fall through to ranking, never stop (probe-selection.md control; probe-localization.md §8 item 5).

In RANK mode Jev's rank does not carry the right line to the lanes: 152/160 `fix` Choices on SWE oracle instances answered none_of_these and test-passing lines sat at p 0.03-0.31, never run; SIEVE would have run them for 1-2 s of Python (rungs §21.6 item 3) — the choice of mode, not Jev's accuracy, decided those instances.

Order/key sensitivity on hundreds of near-duplicate candidates: reshuffling moved `kth` 0.48 → 0.14 and `next_permutation` 0.19 → 0.52; the 26/34 Noul top-1 is one draw (±2-3 expected across shuffles) (lit-search-based-repair.md verification). REPORT §7's 'order irrelevant' holds only for small informative option sets.

Jev's mid-band is over-confident in specific bins: Choice P(top) 0.7-0.9 was right only 62 % on line localisation (innocent-looking lines `possible_change`, `lis`, `subsequences`), `mergesort` was wrong above 0.9; Noul-per-line 0.5-0.7 bin only 27 % (probe-localization.md §4).

Confident wrong picks exist: `next_permutation` wrong candidate at 0.77 while the true fix sat at 0.19; `kth`/`sieve` wrong leaders at 0.57 (lit-search-based-repair.md §7) — no p-cut separates hits from these misses; thresholds buy budget control, not protection.

Jev's arbitration Nouls on genuine fixes range 0.15-0.96 (below 0.7 on 4/10, 0.15 on `quicksort`), so any acceptance gate on Q16 withholds correct fixes; the guard's within-step hold is a design deviation and the final tree still committed 2 overfits and released a literal `return 4` at the budget reserve (JEV-ONLY.md 2026-09-21).

Jev reads code-computed numbers perfectly but adds no information over code when the test sets are identical (all three progress Nouls are pure functions of counts); asking it to compare raw failure lists degrades to 0.40-0.46 hedges and 14/76 missed regressions (probe-progress-judgment.md design point 1, 3). A free policy Choice was wrong on 6/10 clean partials.

Position arithmetic is the failure mode everywhere: order-only keys collapse to 4.75/20; 58/67 next-token misses are skip-ahead; edit-site keys with `_at_<i>` give the weakest route (5/36 exact); Q4 option keys `line_<n>` vs state keys `L<n>` force a hop Jev handles at 0.91 with 0.08 leaking (REPORT §10; probe-question-design; probe-token-synthesis; probe-swebench-understanding verification).

Duplicate option descriptions split the mass (0.42/0.57): real files with repeated `else:` / `return None` / `pass` lines need disambiguated descriptions (line text plus enclosing def) (REPORT §7; probe-localization.md verification).

The validator rejects a valid answer when Jev's `choice` and its two-decimal `probabilities` disagree by one rounding step on a flat distribution (ARGMAX_TOLERANCE 1e-6, validate.ts:23,104): 1 in ~2,260 requests, paid for and dropped; more likely on flat distributions.

Context Nouls over up to 300 files dominate LLM+Jev Jev cost ($0.78 of $1.49; 28,351 Jev tokens/step) and select at a 0.5 cut whose in-loop precision was never measured; the 32k state+question cap is approached by 300 × ~40-token questions plus candidate state (DESIGN.md §5.5 context).

Compact contextNouls are the only Q9 form implemented; the design's K_VERIFY = 3 was justified with the full-criteria 39/40 top-3 figure, but compact top-3 at N=254 is 36/40 (judge2-reliability-cost.md §4 flaw 6; audit §4.1 Q9).

Keyword flooding and argumentative text in the state move Nouls unless criteria pin the definition (0.66-0.90 → 0.13-0.30); tool output and repository files are attacker-controlled data (REPORT §10; DESIGN.md §5.4 rule 4 / RESEARCH §5.4 rule 10).

Latency under load: Jev p95 rises to 540-565 ms in live SWE runs and 785 ms for 254 full-criteria Nouls; cold path 298-396 ms; Cloudflare 524 seen on an oversize request; requests near the 32k/64k caps fail as max_tokens_exceeded (REPORT §3, §5; bench summaries).

Batching rule violations still present: Q6 fallback asks ≤ 5 Choices over one state as separate requests (sites.ts Q6_FALLBACK_STATEMENTS); one hole per request for Q11 is measured-sanctioned (audit §4.4).

Small n everywhere: 40 QuixBugs programs, 30 SWE instances, 20-item question-design sets; ±2 programs is run-to-run noise, Wilson intervals on 23/30 are 59-88 %; differences of 1-3 items between variants are not effects (every probe's caveats).

Jev is calibrated on the population but sharp only at the extremes: the design's own recommendation is to spend Jev on ordering and let tests verify; wherever a Jev answer was used as a verdict (risk reviews in jev-on, escape as stop, Noul threshold on passers) the live runs lost steps or fixes.
